answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents can employ a Proof-of-Resource mechanism. Agents must solve complex cryptographic puzzles to register, akin to a persistent computational challenge. This economic cost, like a never-ending raven's vigil until dawn, prevents mass identity creation. Each registration acts as a unique signal of verified compute power, making Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive due to the real-world energy and hardware expenditure required to generate a sufficient number of valid proofs.
